title: Constructible exceptional mate cocycles
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified six operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Finite inputs used for compact support carry compatible etale-origin witnesses; integral inputs are derived complete with compatible witnessed finite reductions, rational operations are raw localization, and algebraically closed coefficients are represented at a common finite coefficient field. All operations below are restricted to their stated constructible domains; tensor factors and comparisons have their stated finite-Tor hypotheses. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hW$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On each coefficient stage put $F_f=Rf_!$, $G_f=Rf^!$ and use their specified constructible adjunction, with unit $\eta_f$ and counit $\epsilon_f$. Use the canonical compact-support compositors, with their unit and associativity laws. On finite constructible finite-Tor inputs the quotient exceptional comparison is the one preserving the two explicit unit/counit equations of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. At integral coefficients use the coherent constructible adjoint of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], and at rational coefficients and finite scalar extensions those of [lem-coef-rational-operations]. These coefficient comparisons intertwine both Hom transposition maps
$$a:F_fU\to V\longmapsto G_f(a)\eta_{f,U},\qquad b:U\to G_fV\longmapsto\epsilon_{f,V}F_f(b).$$
Successive transposition with $f,g$ agrees with transposition for $F_gF_f\dashv G_fG_g$, whose unit and counit are
$$(G_f\eta_gF_f)\eta_f,\qquad\epsilon_g(F_g\epsilon_fG_g).$$
The inverses $c_{g,f}:G_{gf}\cong G_fG_g$ of the conjugate comparisons $G_fG_g\cong G_{gf}$ of [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-compositor] therefore satisfy the identity and associative cocycle equations; the units and counits obey the displayed composite formulas after these identifications. Coefficient passage preserves these equations and all corresponding well-typed mates of identities and pasted comparison equations. Only the specified constructible exceptional adjoints occur: there is no claim that an arbitrary square mate of an isomorphism is invertible or that an unrestricted ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint exists.

proof.text:
Work throughout in the stated constructible domains. For any allowed coefficient passage write $T_X,T_Y$ for its functors, put primes on the target operations, and write $q:T_YF_f\cong F'_fT_X$, $b:T_XG_f\cong G'_fT_Y$. The constructible coefficient-adjunction theorem supplies precisely these comparisons, both triangle identities, and
$$G'_f(q_U)b_{F_fU}T_X(\eta_{f,U})=\eta'_{f,T_XU},\qquad \epsilon'_{f,T_YV}F'_f(b_V)q_{G_fV}=T_Y(\epsilon_{f,V}).$$
For a finite quotient these are the two displayed equations of lem-coef-finite-exceptional. Integral reduction uses the coherent integral adjunction, whose comparisons identify units and counits with the finite ones. Rationalization and finite scalar extension use the identifications preserving units and counits in lem-coef-rational-operations; the coefficient-adjunction theorem also specifies the common-stage comparisons and their cocycles. Thus these equations concern actual maps of the specified functors, with no assertion about an ambient pro-etale adjoint.

proof.text:
For $a:F_fU\to V$ its transported left-hand arrow is $a'=T_Y(a)q_U^{-1}:F'_fT_XU\to T_YV$. Naturality of $b$ at $a$ and the unit equation of step 1 give
$$b_VT_X(G_f(a)\eta_{f,U})=G'_f(T_Ya)b_{F_fU}T_X\eta_{f,U}=G'_f(a')\eta'_{f,T_XU}.$$
This is the required forward transposition square, not merely agreement on objects.

proof.text:
For $u:U\to G_fV$, put $u'=b_VT_X(u)$. The counit equation of step 1 and naturality of $q$ at $u$ give
$$\epsilon'_{f,T_YV}F'_f(u')=T_Y(\epsilon_{f,V})q_{G_fV}^{-1}F'_f(T_Xu)=T_Y(\epsilon_{f,V}F_f(u))q_U^{-1}.$$
This is the inverse transposition square. The same computations apply to every allowed coefficient functor of step 1, without requiring it to be faithful or a finite quotient to be flat.

proof.text:
Use the composite adjunction $F_gF_f\dashv G_fG_g$. Its Hom bijection is the composite of the two Hom bijections, its unit is $\eta^{g,f}=(G_f\eta_gF_f)\eta_f$, and its counit is $\epsilon^{g,f}=\epsilon_g(F_g\epsilon_fG_g)$. Explicitly, successive transposition of $a:F_gF_fU\to V$ is
$$G_f(G_g(a)\eta_{g,F_fU})\eta_{f,U}=G_fG_g(a)\eta^{g,f}_U;$$
the reverse is $\epsilon^{g,f}_VF_gF_f(u)$. These are exactly the two displayed formulas in the item. The identity adjunction supplies the corresponding identity formulas.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha_{g,f}:F_gF_f\cong F_{gf}$ and $d_{g,f}:G_fG_g\cong G_{gf}$ for the specified conjugate of $\alpha_{g,f}^{-1}$; put $c_{g,f}=d_{g,f}^{-1}$ as in the statement. The constructible compositor node identifies this actual $d$ by its Hom chain and pasted counit. Apply the unit and counit identities for a mate with $L_1=F_gF_f$, $R_1=G_fG_g$, $L_2=F_{gf}$, $R_2=G_{gf}$, identity side functors and square $\alpha_{g,f}^{-1}$. They give
$$d_{g,f,F_gF_fU}\eta^{g,f}_U=G_{gf}(\alpha_{g,f,U}^{-1})\eta_{gf,U},$$
$$\epsilon_{gf,V}F_{gf}(d_{g,f,V})=\epsilon^{g,f}_V\alpha_{g,f,G_fG_gV}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $d$ and cancellation of the inverse isomorphisms rewrite these as
$$c_{g,f,F_{gf}U}\eta_{gf,U}=G_fG_g(\alpha_{g,f,U})\eta^{g,f}_U,$$
$$\epsilon_{gf,V}=\epsilon^{g,f}_V\alpha_{g,f,G_fG_gV}^{-1}F_{gf}(c_{g,f,V}).$$
Hence the original units and counits are precisely the composite ones under the stated identifications.

proof.text:
The finite compact-support compositors are unital and associative by thm-sf-comp-composition; the completed-shriek composition-laws node supplies these same equations for the specified completed integral, raw rational and common-stage compositors. Conjugation is a bijection, sends identities to identities and reverses composition. Pasting along composite adjunctions identifies conjugates of whiskered compositors with the correspondingly whiskered conjugates. Apply these facts to
$$\alpha_{h,gf}(F_h\alpha_{g,f})=\alpha_{hg,f}(\alpha_{h,g}F_f).$$
For $d$ this yields $d_{h,gf}(d_{g,f}G_h)=d_{hg,f}(G_fd_{h,g})$. Invert to obtain
$$(c_{g,f}G_h)c_{h,gf}=(G_fc_{h,g})c_{hg,f}:G_{hgf}\longrightarrow G_fG_gG_h.$$
All these equations use the canonical associators. Conjugating the two left unit equations gives the two right unit equations after the canonical identity-functor identifications. Only conjugates between adjoints to functors with the same source and target are inverted; no arbitrary square mate is asserted invertible.

proof.text:
Coefficient compatibility with the specified $d$ is already stated for finite quotients and finite-free changes by the finite exceptional-compositor coefficient node, and for completed integral, rational and common-stage changes by the adic exceptional-compositor coefficient node. Suppressing components, their equation is
$$b_{gf}T_X(d_{g,f})=d'_{g,f}(G'_fb_g)(b_fG_g).$$
Multiplying by the inverses of $d,d'$ gives the explicit equation for the inverse compositor $c_{g,f}=d_{g,f}^{-1}$:
$$(G'_fb_g)(b_fG_g)T_X(c_{g,f})=c'_{g,f}b_{gf}.$$
Thus coefficient passage carries the actual exceptional compositors, including their unit equations and triple cocycle, to the corresponding maps. At integral coefficients the cited result is an equality of coherent-system maps realized by the total inverse limit; it does not infer equality of derived morphisms from their separate finite evaluations. Rational and common-stage assertions are about the localized and common-stage maps themselves.

proof.text: For a general well-typed comparison square, expand its mate as unit insertion, application of its square map, and counit contraction, using def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate. Steps 2 and 3 commute coefficient passage with each transposition; naturality commutes it with the square map. It therefore commutes with their composite, the mate. For a pasted square, the two pasting formulas of lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting identify the mate of the paste with the paste of the mates, including pasting along composite adjunctions of step 4; the changing-adjunction formulas identify the conjugate comparisons in steps 5-7. Applying this bijection to both sides of any specified identity or pasted comparison equation preserves equality. This proves the last clause for all such well-typed mates. At a common finite coefficient field use the comparisons and cocycles of the coefficient-adjunction theorem, so the result is independent of the chosen representative. No additional ambient adjunction or invertibility statement has entered.
